He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech Red Raiders]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas Jayhawks]]. ==High school career== McCullar played basketball for [[Karen Wagner High School]] in [[San Antonio|San Antonio, Texas]]. As a sophomore, he helped his team reach the Class 6A state title game. In his junior season, McCullar averaged 16.8 points, 6.6 rebounds and 3.8 assists per game, before fracturing his [[tibia]] during the playoffs.{{cite web |last1=Silva Jr. |first1=Carlos |title=McCullar pledges to play for Texas Tech |url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/basketball/2018/07/06/san-antonio-wagner-guard-mccullar-pledges-to-play-for-texas-tech/11589166007/ |website=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=July 5, 2018}} He opted to graduate early and bypass his senior season.{{cite web |last1=Zuvanich |first1=Adam |title=Wagner standout McCullar to skip senior season |url=https://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/high_school/high_school_basketball/article/Wagner-standout-McCullar-to-skip-senior-season-12902434.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=May 9, 2018}} A consensus four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], he committed to playing college basketball for [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] over offers from [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston]], [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]] and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]].{{cite web |last1=Hinojosa |first1=David |title=Wagner's McCullar commits to Texas Tech |url=https://www.expressnews.com/sports/high_school/high_school_boys_basketball/article/Wagner-s-McCullar-commits-to-Texas-Tech-13052806.php |website=[[San Antonio Express-News]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=July 5, 2018}} ==College career== McCullar [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his first season at Texas Tech to rehabilitate after fracturing his tibia as a junior in high school. Despite his absence, his team reached the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship game]].{{cite web |last1=Strader |first1=Jay |title=McCullar finds role for Red Raiders |url=http://www.dailytoreador.com/sports/mccullar-finds-role-for-red-raiders/article_5bfa2ea8-53a2-11ea-b787-9b36b860d0b8.html |website=[[The Daily Toreador]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=February 19, 2020}} As a freshman, McCullar averaged six points, 3.2 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Mainville |first1=Ryan |title=McCullar feeling prepared for new season |url=http://www.dailytoreador.com/sports/mccullar-feeling-prepared-for-new-season/article_ea158530-198a-11eb-9ff5-eb337ed3d258.html |website=[[The Daily Toreador]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=October 28, 2020}} In his sophomore season, he averaged 10.4 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.7 steals per game, earning All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] honorable mention.{{cite web |last1=Marquez |first1=RJ |title=Former SA Wagner standout, Texas Tech star Kevin McCullar Jr. using new NIL laws to build brand, give back to community |url=https://www.ksat.com/news/local/2021/07/19/former-sa-wagner-standout-texas-tech-star-kevin-mccullar-jr-using-new-nil-laws-to-build-brand-give-back-to-community/ |publisher=[[KSAT-TV]] |access-date=December 20, 2021 |date=July 19, 2021}} On November 12, 2021, he scored a career-high 24 points in an 88–62 win against [[Grambling State Tigers men's basketball|Grambling State]].{{cite news |title=Texas Tech overwhelms Grambling in second half, wins 88–62 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401372314 |access-date=December 23, 2021 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 12, 2021}} As a junior, McCullar averaged 10.1 points, 4.6 rebounds, and 3.1 assists per game. He hit 28 of 90 three pointers for 31.1%.{{cite news |last=Bedore |first=Gary |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Former Texas Tech Red Raider Kevin McCullar exits NBA Draft, will play for KU Jayhawks |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/college/big-12/university-of-kansas/article262009540.html |work=[[Kansas City Star]] |location=[[Kansas City, Missouri]] |access-date=June 2, 2022}} On April 27, 2022, he entered the [[NCAA transfer portal|transfer portal]] while also declaring for the [[2022 NBA draft]] and maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last1=Silva Jr. |first1=Carlos |title=Texas Tech basketball player Kevin McCullar enters name into the NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.lubbockonline.com/story/sports/college/red-raiders/2022/04/27/texas-tech-basketball-player-kevin-mccullar-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal/9557268002/ |website=[[Lubbock Avalanche-Journal]] |access-date=May 19, 2022 |date=April 27, 2022}} On May 19, 2022, McCullar announced he was transferring to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] while also remaining in the NBA draft.{{Cite web |title=Texas Tech’s Kevin McCullar Announces Decision to Transfer to Kansas |url=https://www.si.com/college/2022/05/20/texas-tech-kevin-mccullar-announces-transfer-kansas-nba-draft|first=Madison|last= Williams|date=May 19, 2022|access-date=May 19, 2022|website=Sports Illustrated}} On June 1, 2022, McCullar removed himself from the NBA Draft and announced he would be playing for the Jayhawks.{{cite news |last=Guskey |first=Jordan |date=June 1, 2022 |title=Kevin McCullar announces he’s exiting NBA draft process, returning to college at Kansas |url=https://www.cjonline.com/story/sports/college/hawk-zone/2022/06/01/kevin-mccullar-texas-tech-nba-draft-2022-ku-kansas-basketball/7470835001/ |work=[[Topeka Capital-Journal]] |location=[[Topeka, Kansas]] |access-date=June 2, 2022}} As a senior, he was named to the Third Team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] as well as the All-Defensive Team.{{cite web |title=🏀 Jayhawk Starters Headline 2023 All-Big 12 Honors for Kansas |url=https://kuathletics.com/jayhawk-starters-headline-2023-all-big-12-honors-for-kansas/ |website=[[Kansas Jayhawks]] |access-date=March 6, 2023 |date=March 5, 2023 |archive-date=December 4, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231204180122/https://kuathletics.com/jayhawk-starters-headline-2023-all-big-12-honors-for-kansas/ |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== On June 27, 2024, McCullar was selected with the 56th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]], however, immediately on draft night, he was traded to the [[New York Knicks]].{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Davis|title=Johnny Furphy, Kevin McCullar Taken in Second Round of NBA Draft|url=https://www.si.com/college/kansas/basketball/johnny-furphy-kevin-mccullar-taken-in-second-round-of-nba-draft-01j1bad33rwb|work=Sports Illustrated|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}} On August 5, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Knicks.{{cite web|title=New York Knicks Sign Kevin McCullar Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/new-york-knicks-sign-kevin-mccullar-jr-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 5, 2024|access-date=August 5, 2024}} On March 25, 2025, McCullar made his NBA debut, and scored his first two career points in a 128–113 victory over the [[2024–25 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web | last=Bondy | first=Stefan | title=Knicks' Kevin McCullar Jr. scores first two points in NBA debut after long, arduous road | website=New York Post | date=2025-03-26 | url=https://nypost.com/2025/03/26/sports/knicks-kevin-mccullar-jr-scores-first-two-points-in-nba-debut/ | access-date=2025-12-06}} On December 27, 2025, McCullar had his career best game yet, as he recorded career highs in several statistical categories. Scoring 13 points, grabbing 8 rebounds, 4 of them offensive, 2 assists and 2 steals, whilst also going 3-of-6 from three-point range in 23 minutes in a 128-125 road victory over the [[2025–26 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]]. Which earned him glowing praise from Knicks Head Coach [[Mike Brown (basketball, born 1970)|Mike Brown]] in the post-game press conference, who commended McCullar’s defense, effort and mentality in being ready to step up when needed for his team. He was also voted Defensive Player Of The Game for the first time by his fellow Knicks teammates and coaches. On June 13, 2026, McCullar and the Knicks won the [[2026 NBA Finals]], beating the [[San Antonio Spurs]] 4–1.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nba/new-york-knicks/knicks-news-first-championship-53-years-nba-finals-spurs|title=Knicks win first championship in 53 years after NBA Finals Game 5 triumph vs.
